newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr, forward premia up.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady vs dlr, forward premia up.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Thursday at 35.83/84 per dollar, marginally up from the opening 35.84/86 while forward premia ended sharply higher, dealers said.
They said the rupee traded at 35.83 and a low of 35.855 per dollar on Thursday. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought dollars at 35.835 rupees, they said.

"Some short-covering in the morning pushed the rupee down to 35.85/86," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "It remained at that level for quite some time before dollar supplies helped it retrace to 35.82/83."
He said RBI dollar purchases then nudged the rupee down to the closing levels.
Dealers said premia on forward dollars went up sharply on paying pressure and lack of receiving interest from the RBI.

The RBI has been rolling over swaps since earlier this month, receiving premia and keeping sentiment in the forward market soft. Its receiving has acted as a balancing factor to the paying pressure from banks and importers, dealers said.
"Its absence from the market today pushed up rates as there continued to be the normal paying," a dealer said.
Forward on six-month dollars ended Thursday at an annualised 7.59 percent against Wednesday's closing 7.37 percent.
